title: Tor amplitude of a quasi-coherent complex is tested on quasi-coherent modules
statement: Let X be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], let E be an object of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], and let a\le b be integers. If H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal F)=0 for all i\notin[a,b] and every quasi-coherent \mathcal O_X-module \mathcal F, then E has tor amplitude in [a,b]: H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G)=0 for all i\notin[a,b] and every \mathcal O_X-module \mathcal G.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 36.10.6 (Tag 08EA; label lemma-tor-qc-qs), implication (2) => (1)

proof.text: Choose standard derived localizations independently on each open subscheme. Reuse tensor_vanishes_iff from the existing TorAmplitudeOpenLocal module through a proof-only import all. Its proved K-flat resolution and tensor comparisons identify the existential vanishing predicate with zero cohomology of the actual derived tensor.

For an affine open U, exact derived restriction preserves quasi-coherent cohomology by the open-restriction criterion. An affine scheme is compact, so its inclusion into quasi-separated X is quasi-compact; its open immersion is quasi-separated. Push a quasi-coherent module F on U to X, where it remains quasi-coherent. Apply the global test hypothesis and restrict its zero cohomology. The open tensor comparison, exact cohomology comparison, single-functor comparison and the open-immersion counit identify the result with the local derived tensor against F. Thus all local quasi-coherent test modules satisfy the same bounds.
Apply the proved affine quasi-coherent Tor-amplitude detection theorem to the restricted object. This supplies vanishing for every module on each affine open.

Fix a global module G and a degree outside the interval. The open tensor and exact cohomology comparisons transport local vanishing for G restricted to U to zero restrictions of the global tensor cohomology. Mathlib iSup_affineOpens_eq_top gives the cover, and the proved source Scheme.Modules.isZero_of_iSup_eq_top detects zero from these restrictions. The K-flat vanishing equivalence yields the original existential predicate.
